video_title: Wemby said WHAT about Jared McCain?! 'It do look SUSPICIOUS!' - Perk | The Pat McAfee Show

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins recounts heated AAU game altercation defending his player
quotes.excerpt: After the game, he comes and he body slams one of my kids that play for my team.
quotes.quote: No, so so let me give you the details real quick. It's my organization, right, Young Perkins Global, and we were in a tournament, it's a heated game, you know, 17U, they're going back and forth whatever. We end up winning the game, all right, cool. Well, the other team, they have they had this guy that's like 7 foot, 400 pounds. After the game, he comes and he body slams one of my one of my kids that play for my team. So I stay seated, then I get up because everybody running around, the players they about to fight. So as a responsible, owner of the organization, I get up and I'm like, 'Hey man, y'all need to chill,' you know, X, Y and Z. I'm grabbing my players. I tell the coach of the other team, I'm like, 'Hey bro, get your players, I got mine.' He pop off. And I ain't getting nothing. I ain't getting nothing. 'Who the hell are you?' I'm like, 'Bro, just get your players so I can get mine, we get up out of here.' He said it, he got smart with me again. That's when I got pissed off. I'm like, 'Bro, who the hell are you talking to?' 'Man, I'm talking to you.' So then all of a sudden, you know, boo boo boo boo boo. Now, what people didn't see was after that, we had a little exchange, yeah, they held us back or whatever, held them back, held me back. And then afterwards, we dabbed up, he said my bad, I said my bad and we kept it moving.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins explains his duty to protect players
quotes.excerpt: His parents trust me with their child. So I got to protect that child as if he's mine.
quotes.quote: His parents wasn't at the game. So his parents trust me with their child. So I got to protect that child as if he's mine. I'm going to stand up for him, even though I didn't go over there with bad intentions, I got to make sure that that kid is okay and he make it back home to his parents. He's a young man, but again, he plays in my organization. So I got to make sure by every means necessary that he's safe.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins addresses the widespread flopping problem in the NBA playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I do think we have a bit of a flopping problem all around the league.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat's co-host
text_blocks.text: Like genuinely Perk, when you see, you know, McCain go down, and just fall on his face, or you see, I think it was Williams run into Johnson last night and then just fall back and get those fouls called. Like, what are your actual thoughts? Because at a certain point, and not even the SGA stuff from what people complain about, but like, stuff like this, when you see that as someone who is again, just watching because you want is the Western Conference Finals, this is the stuff you're going to be, basically talking about and you're on a trip to the finals. But when you see that as an old school guy, like, how does that not grind your gears just a little bit?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: It does. It does because I want the games to be decided by the players, not by the officials. And I do think we have a bit of a flopping problem all around the league, to be honest with you. If you go back and look at the start of since the start of the playoffs, every single time a guy all if I'm a coach, I'm telling guys, 'Hey man, run real hard if someone trying to set a screen for you on you and just fall to the ground. You'll get the call.' So yes, it is an area that we have to clean up. But it's not just SGA, it's not just the Oklahoma City Thunder. I didn't seen Wemby try to sell calls, I didn't seen Stephon Castle try to sell calls.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins attributes Wemby's playoff struggles to exhaustion and learning process
quotes.excerpt: This is a learning process for Wemby and he got to go through it.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat's co-host
text_blocks.text: What's your thoughts on his up and down performances? We all remember the first game where everybody was comparing him to Shaq or Hakeem, Tim Duncan, having a dominant performance. But now what do you think? Having the game last night, a couple games ago, I think he had like four or five rebounds. What's your thoughts on that? And what are the teammates or coaching staff maybe saying to him? Because I hear guys like Shump, he said a story one time where LeBron was leading everybody every category and Ty Lue came in the locker room and said, 'Hey, we need more.' So we know what kind of pressure these guys have on their shoulders. So what's the thoughts? What are the conversations right now in the Spurs locker room when it comes to Wemby?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Well, with Wemby, I would say this, as expected, right? We're talking about this is the Conference Finals. This is a deep run. Do you know the physicality and the toll on Wemby's body? I think Wemby in the regular season averaged about 28, 29 minutes. Last night he played 38. So he's playing a lot of minutes. The Oklahoma City Thunder are sending multiple big guys at you, the physicality, you got one day in between now with the games, the travel. So this is a learning process. Last night he looked exhausted. Half of it had to do with the physicality of the Oklahoma City Thunder. The other half is just youth and going through these growing pains. This is a learning process for Wemby and he got to go through it.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins argues Wemby needs a reliable 'Robin' to win a championship
quotes.excerpt: We have never in the history of the game seen someone get crowned a champion without having a Robin.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Can anyone tell me right now who is his Robin? Because I know every Batman that didn't won a championship had a reliable Robin. Who is his Robin on his team right now?

text_blocks.speaker: Pat's co-host
text_blocks.text: I think Castle would be the answer there. I think.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: No, you can't you can't ask Castle to be the Robin when his responsibility is to guard SGA. What I'm saying is this, we know that. No, that's not an easy task. It's tough. What I'm saying is this. In order to get where you're trying to go, and that's to the promised land, we have never in the history of the game seen someone get crowned a champion without having a Robin on their side to have to pick up the lifting, the heavy part, especially when you're on the road.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins criticizes Chet Holmgren's road performance and fear of moment
quotes.excerpt: We've been asking for Chet to do it, but obviously he looked afraid of the moment at times.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: That's why OKC got smoked in Game 4, because the game plan was surrounded by SGA and then all of a sudden, who was there for him to step up? Jay Dub was out, AJ Mitchell was out. We've been asking for Chet to do it, but obviously he looked afraid of the moment at times.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat
text_blocks.text: No, now you said he had a double-double last night, quietly. You literally just said Holmgren, you said.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat
text_blocks.text: Okay, you're saying on the road he needs to show up. Okay, I got you.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins criticizes Kenny Atkinson's 'organizational' answers and Cavs' embarrassing exit
quotes.excerpt: How the Cavs went out as a whole, like disjointed, disconnected, no passion, was like a huge embarrassment to the NBA.
quotes.quote: No, because every answer was an organizational answer, if that makes sense, from Kenny Atkinson. When they asked him about James Harden and his defense after Game 1 and Kenny Atkinson had the audacity to say, 'Hey, James Harden has been one of our better defenders.' And he got his ass tore up in Game 1 by Jalen Brunson and the rest of the New York Knicks. Right then, what came to mind is that, 'Oh yeah, I forgot. You all got a verbal agreement with James Harden that you all going to give him a contract extension after the season.' Great job, Kenny. Way to protect the organization. And then on top of that, he come with that asinine statement of, 'Yeah, we won the analytics.' What? What? You won the analytics? Where's your like, where's the leadership in that locker room? I and you know, it's not what you do, it's how you do it. I don't listen, I picked the Knicks to win the series, but how the Cavs went out as a whole, like disjointed, disconnected, no passion, was like a huge embarrassment to the NBA. Like, it was a huge embarrassment, man.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins questions James Harden's desire to win a championship
quotes.excerpt: It's a fair question. It's a real question because we want to know.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat's co-host
text_blocks.text: How much does James Harden want to win an NBA championship? Is that fair to ask, Perk?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Yes. No, but it's a fair question. It's a real question because we want to know. Because it's no, it's no way that James Harden has these drop-offs in the postseason when it matters the most like he do. Again, all throughout the playoffs, it was the same story, different series. More turnovers than made field goals. A lack of effort defensively. James Harden, last time I checked, you were brought in to be not only a valuable piece to get them where they were trying to go, but also to be a leader. I didn't see leadership out there. They were searching for leadership and when Donovan Mitchell tried and they showed the camera view on the bench of him yelling at the team, guys were drowning him out. So all I'm saying is, they fired JB Bickerstaff for less, is what I'm saying.
